verdict.stance: Constructive / COMESA Multilateral Trade Bank with 35% CAR (BB / Ba1)
verdict.summary: TDB Group (the Eastern & Southern African COMESA multilateral trade bank) manages ~$10bn+ assets with a fortress ~35% CAR (vs 30% statutory floor), ~$170.5m+ annual earnings, and preferred creditor status (PCS). Fitch BB / Moody's Ba1 ratings balance exceptional capitalization against sovereign arrears in Zambia/South Sudan.

positives: Multilateral treaty institution with Preferred Creditor Status (PCS) across 25+ African member states.
Exceptional ~35% Capital Adequacy Ratio (vs 30% statutory floor) and ~$10bn+ asset scale.
Core private-sector Stage 3 NPLs contained at ~3.2% (total NPL ~3.7%).
negatives: Exposure to distressed African sovereigns (Zambia, South Sudan, Ethiopia) creates Stage 2/3 arrears drag.
Concentrated member-state sovereign shareholder credit quality vs higher-rated MDB peers.
2028 $650m Eurobond (XS2356571559) refinancing window requires sustained DFI & market access.

background.business_overview: Treaty-based regional multilateral development and trade finance bank for Eastern & Southern Africa.
background.asset_perimeter: ~$10bn+ assets financing sovereign trade, infrastructure, agribusiness, and SMEs across COMESA/EAC/SADC.
background.ownership_governance: 26 member states (incl. Kenya, Egypt, Ethiopia, Mauritius) + institutional Class B shareholders (AfDB, China PBOC, European DFIs).

recent_drivers: Balance sheet crossed $10bn milestone (from $9.9bn, $7.3bn gross portfolio, $170.5m profit, 35.9% CAR).
Fitch affirmed TDB at BB Stable (Moody's Ba1, GCR BBB+) noting strong capital & PCS vs sovereign restructurings.

catalysts.impact: Monitors Zambia/Ethiopia sovereign restructuring recoveries and CAR.

management_guidance_tracker.management_target: CAR >30% statutory floor; expand Class B/C equity
management_guidance_tracker.variance_analysis: Strong capital cushion absorbs sovereign restructuring provisions.

management_questions.question: Quantify carrying value and restructuring recovery status on Zambia, Ethiopia, and South Sudan sovereign exposures.
